comment: Professor Shannon is likely fine if you have taken calculus before, but if you have not, I would strongly recommend you take a different professor. She does not teach to the lowest common denominator in the class, and clearly gears her lectures towards students who have already taken calculus. Also, she is virtually inaccessible outside of class.

Took Shannon my first semester and had her class twice a week. I cried twice a week. Shannon regurgitates straight from the textbook and the tests are impossible. Homework on WebAssign after every class and it's hard. Even my friends in calc two struggled to help me. You probably shouldn't take her class, but I guess if you have to... good luck
Makes calculus way too hard and has no interest in seeing any of her students succeed. Test averages are consistently in the 60's and there is no curve. Do not take her class.

She goes wayyyyyyy too fast especially for students unfamiliar with calculus. Didn't like way she explained things, just rehashes what the book says and I don't like professors who do that. Lots of homework. If you're relatively new to calc, avoid her unless you really need the credit. If you're good at calc and just need the credit you can get by.
Reasonable workload, reasonable pace especially for someone unfamiliar with Calculus, better than most of the alternatives in the math department

Shannon FLIES through material and never reviews anything the day after. Doesn't relate any lectures to one another. Reviews in class before each test are extremely useless, as she just skims over topics in the lectures. Tests are unnecessarily difficult, and way harder than any practice she gives. If you aren't math oriented, do not take her class

FLIES THROUGH MATERIAL AS IF IT WERE A RACE! I took calc in high school and am still finding it difficult to keep up. Review sessions that she holds before tests are useless and she doesn't even go over half the stuff on the test. Makes tests that take too long to complete and often doesn't give you enough time to finish quizzes.

There are few things i learned from this course, the most important being that Professor Shannon is a lowly spiteful creature. throughout the duration of the course she made us feel like a hapless wanderer, like explorers without a map, ships without a rudder, like lions led by a sheep.

Kim Shannon is an awesome, caring professor. She is very straight forward with concepts and in her lectures and her grading system helps the students a lot. Homework, classwork, and quizzes are plentiful and are a great way to boost your grade. Tests can be a little hard but if you take notes in class and study you should be fine.
Calc professor that flies through all material. If you took Calc in High School you're good but if not...

Professor Shannon is professional, goes over everything you need to know for her tests/quizzes, and will do what she can to help out all students. Yes, the course itself is very difficult and fast-paced like all college calculus courses are, but she will help you outside of class if you ask. I struggled, but Professor Shannon was there to help.
I took calc senior year, so her class was pretty easy for me. She's straightforward, is receptive to questions, and seems to be available a lot. She's sassy in a good way.

One couldn't ask for a teacher that care more about her students. She is 120% available to help you with any problem you have on an assignment and tweaks the grading scheme in the students favor. However, tests contain stuff that is much tougher than whats covered in class and the tempo in which the material is covered is insanely fast.

Definitely take Shannon. If you're scared because it's Calc, don't be. I had no calc experience prior to this class and I'm doing fine. Keys to success: Show up to class, take good (clear) notes, and do the odd number problems on your own time. Above all,  anchor down for the tests!!! If that's not your style though, consider a different prof.

She is very nice, I am in her class and so far I have an 89% with minimal effort. She would answer any questions in class without hesitation. Her exams are somehow hard to be honest, but she does put a lot of effort into helping us practice by giving revision and homework sheets. I was hoping to take Calc II with her, too bad she doesn't teach it.

I took college level Calculus I and II in High School, unfortunately they did not transfer. So I thought this course would be simple. Wrong.  Professor Shannon can not explain the most simple concepts of Calculus without getting almost the entire class confused. Also her homework assignments resemble minimal to her notes, so be prepared.

Mrs. Shannon is not a good teacher. I was able to do well in her class only because I am good at math as well as teaching concepts to myself. She was not able to explain concepts clearly and tested us with problems that were never discussed during class

If you want to get a good grade (an A), don't take her unless u have taken calc before and done well in high school. The examples she gives us are totally different from the homework and the homework is totally different from the test. Really bad Calc professor ruined my GPA that semester. Doesn't explain things plus bad office hours. Stay away!
Avoid if possible.  Her lectures do not help with the WebAssign homework.  The exams are different from the homework, and different from the lectures.

She comes off helpful, but then you realize she has terrible office hours and does not really explain things clearly when you go. I cannot tell you how many times my classmates and I have walked out of that class and felt like everything was an incomprehensible blur. Her tests are nothing like the homework, and her final was incredibly impossible.

SHE'S  NOT A PROFESSOR. She is just a teacher and teaches horribly. I got an A in Calculus in high school and now I am doing so poorly in her class. Office hours suck. Tests are hard.  Surprisingly she's the better one out of the Calc 1 teachers.
She is very nice and helpful.

Kim Shannon is the best of the UR Calc 1 teachers. This is undeniable. She is a great professor and has a lot of energy. Class is almost always engaging. She definitely is more difficult than other professors, but it helps you for the final. Only thing is that her tests are brutally difficult sometimes. An A in the class is not unreasonable.

she's a great teacher. i understand everything crystal clear in class. but for some reasons she makes her test so incredibly hard so everyone does badly and she has to give us extra points. sighhhhh good luck with her

Not clear, not helpful.  Gets her own examples wrong and is not at all helpful in preparing you for her own exams.  Homeworks are easy but graded by students so there are often mistakes which can hurt your grade if you're not careful.  I'd say avoid if possible.

Extremely helpful during office hours. Teaches directly from textbook. Some tests questions are random and difficult. Important to do hw correctly and do well on quizzes. Not an easy class, but if you put the work in you should be fine.

ESCAPE WHILE YOU CAN. Unless, of course, you WANT to get a D. I took calc in high school and got an A. Got a C in her class. The tests are impossible that even she gets the questions wrong when we review them in class. DO NOT TAKE.

Available outside class and extremely helpful, BUT her tests have nothing to do with what you learn in class, they are completely different and DONT take this class unless you had a really good calc class in high school. If you've never taken calculus, get outtt.

Kim Shannon is really nice and helpful. she is there to help whenever you ask for help during her office hours and even by e-mail. When it comes to easiness, however, she gives lots of homework. But, homework really helps in the tests. If you will have time to do the homework and spend a bit of time on math, then I recommend her.
